card.title: Short Story 1 — The Selfish Giant (Oscar Wilde)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: 'The Selfish Giant' is Oscar Wilde's fairy-tale allegory in which a giant walls off his beautiful garden and keeps the children out, so that winter takes permanent possession of the grounds. When he finally lets the children return, spring comes back, the rose tree blossoms and the giant discovers lasting happiness in sharing.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
The giant built a wall around his beautiful garden, keeping the children out.
Because the children were excluded, winter perpetually reigned in the garden.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ The giant was always kind. ✅ He was selfish at first, then transformed.  ·  ❌ The story is just about a garden. ✅ It's a spiritual allegory about love and redemption.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The giant was NOT always kind - he was selfish at first and then transformed; do not write otherwise.  ·  The story is NOT just about a garden - it is a spiritual allegory about love and redemption.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Summarize 'The Selfish Giant' in 100 words.  ·  What is the symbolism of winter and spring in the story?

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Treat the seasons as a moral thermometer: winter = selfishness, spring = compassion. Always state the pairing in symbolism answers.  ·  Do not omit the little boy, whose tears bring spring back and who represents Christ.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Summarize 'The Selfish Giant' in about 100 words.  ·  Explain the symbolism of winter and spring in the story.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Cause-and-effect chain to memorize: children excluded leads to winter; children admitted leads to spring.  ·  Symbol pairs: wall = ego, winter = selfishness, spring = compassion, rose tree = renewal, little boy = Christ.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: How does the giant change throughout the story?  ·  Discuss the theme of redemption in 'The Selfish Giant'.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: MCQ traps: options saying the giant was always kind, or that the story is only about a garden, are false.  ·  Short-answer areas: the theme of redemption and the symbolism of the garden.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The wall the giant builds, symbolizing separation, ego and isolation  ·  Winter as the coldness of selfishness and spring as the warmth of compassion  ·  The little boy as a Christ-like figure whose tears bring spring back  ·  Redemption: the giant changes from selfish to generous

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Plot: the giant builds a wall around the garden, winter reigns, the children are restored, spring returns and the giant becomes happy.  ·  Characters: the Giant, the Children and the Little Boy.  ·  Themes: selfishness versus generosity, redemption, nature and morality, and childhood innocence.  ·  Symbols: the wall (separation, ego, isolation), winter (selfishness), spring (compassion), the rose tree and the little boy (divine love and Christ).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain the significance of the wall in the story.  ·  Why is the little boy described as a Christ-like figure?

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Use exactly the three characters named in the notes - the Giant, the Children and the Little Boy - when a question asks about characters.  ·  Do not add events or characters that are not supported by the notes.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Why did winter perpetually reign in the giant's garden? → A  ·  The little boy in the story is best described as: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 1. Summary  ·  The Selfish Giant is a tale about a giant who builds a wall around his beautiful garden, keeping children out. As a result, winter perpetually reigns in his garden. When the giant finally lets the children back in, spring returns. Through the story, Wilde explores themes of selfishness, redemption, and the transformative power of love and compassion.  ·  ### 2. Characters

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The children as symbols of innocence, joy and renewal  ·  The rose tree that never blossoms for the selfish giant  ·  Moral: true happiness comes from sharing and loving others.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Exam focus: who built the wall, what the children represent, why winter came, plus short answers on redemption and the symbolism of the garden.  ·  In short answers, name the character, the change and the symbol together, for example the giant, the wall and the returning spring.  ·  When the giant let the children back into the garden, spring returned.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The giant was not always kind; he was selfish at first and later transformed.  ·  The story is a spiritual allegory about love and redemption, not merely a story about a garden.  ·  True happiness comes from sharing and loving others, while selfishness leads to isolation and spiritual winter.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: For theme questions always name two opposing ideas, such as selfishness versus generosity, not only one.  ·  Answer 'why did winter come?' in one line: because the giant built a wall and kept the children out of his garden.  ·  For a 100-word summary use five beats: wall, winter, children return, spring, happiness.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Describe how the giant changes throughout the story.  ·  Identify the characters and state the role each one plays.  ·  - **The Giant**: Initially selfish, later becomes kind and selfless
